newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-SPANISH CHAMPIONSHIP GAMES THIS WEEKEND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SPANISH CHAMPIONSHIP GAMES THIS WEEKEND.

text.p: Spanish championship games this weekend (league standings in parentheses, kickoff times GMT):

Champions Atletico Madrid started their marathon of 10 games in 35 days with a win against Logrones, while Hercules have suffered a dressing-room mutiny and the club board is again under fire after slipping to bottom place.

Both sides had good midweek results -- Celta took a point at third-placed Betis, while Rayo ended the unbeaten record of neighbours and leaders Real Madrid. Celta midfielder Daniel Dutuel doubtful because of injury.
Extremadura hope to continue their recovery against fellow strugglers Espanyol after leaving the top division's basement for the first time this season after Wednesday's draw at Oviedo.
A game between two sides desperate for points that is all the more vital because of the Spanish system in which results between sides level on points at the end of the season decide league positions.

Real will be without suspended central defenders Fernando Hierro and Rafael Alkorta in their bid to recover from Wednesday's shock defeat at struggling Rayo Vallecano. Oviedo have Paulo Bento and striker Manel back from injury.
Former Real Madrid coach Benito Floro saw his side lose 5-0 at Zaragoza on Wednesday and is likely to face dismissal unless Sporting beat Tenerife.
After Wednesday's defeat at Racing Santander, Valladolid coach Vicente Cantatore will make changes in midfield for a game that is crucial to both side's European aspirations.

Coach Luis Fernandez has breathed new life into Athletic and striker Ismael Urzaiz over the past few games, while Uruguayan striker Fernando Correa has done the same for Racing. Another vitally important clash for UEFA Cup places.

Traditionally a high-scoring fixture and a chance for Zaragoza to confirm their recovery and also avenge the controversial 5-3 defeat inflicted by Barcelona earlier this season. Barcelona now six points off the pace following 2-0 defeat at Real Sociedad on Thursday, further increasing problems of British coach Bobby Robson.

Deportivo look a good outside bet for the title again after the superb 3-1 win at Hercules on Wednesday. They will be out to repeat September's victory at Betis, who are still unbeaten away, but are without suspended striker Pier Cherubino.

The last time Compostela striker Lyuboslav Penev returned to his old club he had a fight with club chairman Paco Roig, who is now under fire because of Valencia's run of home draws. Valencia have never lost to Compostela at home.
